processing_notes: Source states: 'According to surveillance data obtained from the Epidemiology Division, Federal Ministry of Health, between January 2004 and December 2008, outbreaks of cholera have been reported in 12 out of the 36 States in the country with 74,881 cases and 1,387 reported deaths (Unpublished data).' - interpreted as 74881 sCh cases, 1387 deaths. REPLACES retracted index 6, which carried these same figures against metadata index 8 'Federal Ministry of Health Nigeria' whose only URL was the bare domain https://www.health.gov.ng - an unverifiable citation. The primary text was located by a Europe PMC full-text search on the literal string '74,881' and is Dalhat et al., Pan African Medical Journal 2018;30:5 (PMC6093587), which attributes the figure to FMoH Epidemiology Division UNPUBLISHED data. [AGENT 5 CONFLICT ADJUDICATION 2026-09-21] THIS FIGURE IS 4.5x THE AUTHORITATIVE ANNUAL SERIES FOR THE SAME WINDOW. The WHO Annual Cholera Report series carried in ./data/NGA/cholera_data_jhu.csv gives 2004 3186/185, 2005 4477/174, 2006 2028/127, 2007 1661/48, 2008 5410/247 - a five-year total of 16,762 cases and 781 deaths, CFR 4.66 percent, against this row's 74,881 and 1,387, CFR 1.85 percent. Both figures are recorded and NEITHER IS AVERAGED. ADJUDICATION: the WHO annual series is PRIMARY for 2004-2008 and this row is NON-PRIMARY, downweighted from 0.7 to 0.4. Rule applied: WHO official over ministry, published over unpublished, and a series over a single relayed aggregate. processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 1974-01-03..1974-02-28. Surveillance is recorded as PARTIAL, not operational, because what is demonstrated is national notification to WHO, not active case-finding in this particular state. processing_notes: Source states: 'In 2024, the pattern changed with Fune recording the highest burden in absolute case counts, contributing 236 (45.2%) of total cases for the year with an incidence rate of 5 per 10,000 population. Confidence lowered to 0.75 from the Level-1 band because the source is an unreviewed preprint. District subset - do not sum with state or national row.
